correctItems.text: • Symbols for chemical elements are written in normal/roman (upright) type.
• The attached numerals specifying a nuclide are placed as a left subscript (atomic number) and superscript (mass number).
For example, a U-235 nuclide is expressed as 92 235U (with 235 expressing the mass number and 92 as the atomic number of uranium with chemical symbol U).
• The right superscript position is used, if required, for indicating a state of ionisation (in case of ions).

correctItems.text: • Standard and recommended symbols for units are written in lower case roman (upright) type, starting with small letters.
The shorter designations for units such as kg, m, s, cd, etc., are symbols and not the abbreviations.
However, the unit symbols are capitalised only if the symbol for a unit is derived from a proper name of scientist, beginning with a capital, normal/roman letter.
The single exception is L, which is the symbol for the unit 'litre'.
